Why it matters

Legal hours come from the sun, and the sun moves fast in the fall. Know your light, your normal weather and what changes each week, and you plan days that work.

  • Near Heffley Creek, October loses almost 2 hours of daylight 90%.

More: the key points in full
  • "To hunt game, except migratory game birds from one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise" is unlawful (99%, synopsis page 11, item 38).
  • "To hunt migratory game birds from 1/2 hour after sunset to 1/2 hour before sunrise" is unlawful (99%, item 37).
  • "The responsibility remains with the hunter to make the determination of sunrise and sunset in the field based on existing terrain and circumstances" (99%, item 38).
  • On 1 November 2026, clocks that would usually turn back stay the same; BC's new time zone is UTC minus 7 (95%, BC government news release, 2 March 2026). Some southeast BC communities follow Alberta 95%; your areas are on BC time.
  • Sun times in this lesson are calculated for 2026 on UTC minus 7, accurate to a minute or two on flat ground 90%. Mountains block the sun earlier: the hunter decides in the field 99%.
  • Weather numbers are 1991 to 2020 Environment Canada climate normals (95%, read directly).

• 1 November 2026: BC clocks stay put 95%.
  • So November sunrise is about 8:15 am near Heffley Creek on 15 November, not 7:15 90%.
More: the time zone change in full
  • BC government release, 2 March 2026: "Spring forward" on 8 March 2026 was the last time change 95%.
  • New time zone: seven hours behind Coordinated Universal Time (UTC minus 7) 95%.
  • On 1 November 2026, clocks "would usually be turned back, but now will remain the same" 95%.
  • Northeast BC (Dawson Creek, Fort St. John) stays on UTC minus 7; southeast BC (Golden, Cranbrook, Invermere) keeps switching to match Alberta 95%.
  • Older apps, newspapers, printed tables or US websites may still show times one hour earlier for November. If a sunrise time looks an hour early, check it (Tip).
  • Washington State still falls back: from November, the border towns south of the Fraser Valley are one hour behind BC (80%, news reports).

Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
  • Work out the start and stop time the night before (Tip).
  • In the field, the hunter decides sunrise and sunset by terrain 99%.
More: the rules in full
Item 38, page 11

"To hunt game, except migratory game birds from one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise. To find out the time of sunrise and sunset, consult a local newspaper or the following website www.nrc-cnrc.gc.ca/eng/services/sunrise/index.html. The responsibility remains with the hunter to make the determination of sunrise and sunset in the field based on existing terrain and circumstances."

Item 37, page 11

"To hunt migratory game birds from 1/2 hour after sunset to 1/2 hour before sunrise."

  • Plain English: deer, quail and grouse: 1 hour before sunrise to 1 hour after sunset. Ducks and geese: half an hour 99%.
  • No lights to hunt (99%, item 38). Tracking after dark: Blood trailing.
  • Quail are not migratory game birds; the 1 hour rule applies to them (95%, my reading of the Schedule and item 38).

More: how these were worked out
  • Point used: Heffley Creek base in this app, 50.86 N, 120.27 W (approximate centre).
  • Method: NOAA general solar position equations, standard sunrise (sun's upper edge on a flat horizon with refraction), clock on UTC minus 7 90%.
  • Check any date with the NRC (National Research Council) sunrise calculator named in the synopsis (99% that it is the named source).
  • Valleys and timbered slopes go dark before official sunset; ridges get light later in the morning. The hunter decides in the field 99%.
  • Field Mode in this app shows today's times: Field Mode.

More: elevation in full
  • The standard atmosphere cools about 6.5 °C per 1,000 m; real days vary a lot (Tip, textbook average).
  • Snow lies on high benches long before it reaches the Kamloops valley (Tip). Deer have trouble in snow deeper than about 30 cm (85%, from Weather, moon and what moves game).
  • Cold air drains downhill at night and pools in hollows (75%, see Wind and thermals).
  • Forecast tip: look at a mountain or point forecast for your bench, not only the city forecast (Tip).

More: season timing in full
  • Snow and cold, not the rut, trigger mule deer migration to winter range (85%, from Weather, moon and what moves game).
  • In the BC Wildlife Federation mule deer study most collared deer migrated in October to November (85%, same lesson).
  • Rut: mid November to mid December; bucks move more and in daylight (75 to 80%, same lesson).
  • Region 3 any buck ends 31 October; 4 point bucks 1 November to 10 December (99%, The BC hunter's year).
  • Ducks: freeze up pushes birds off small water; Fraser Valley ducks run into January (99% for dates; movement: see How animals move through the year).

Grandpa's rule (wisdom, not law)

Grandpa's rule (wisdom): The sun sets the clock, the mountain sets the light. Be in your spot early and leave with light to spare.

Common mistakes
  • Using an old sunrise time in November.
  • Trusting the town forecast for the high benches.
  • Starting the walk out at sunset.
More: the mistakes in full
  • Old printed or US tables show November times one hour earlier than BC clocks now read (95% for the time zone fact).
  • Kamloops valley numbers are not the bench. Expect colder and snowier up high (Tip).
  • In November, legal light ends near 6 pm and full dark comes fast. Plan the walk out with a headlamp (Tip and 90% for the times).

Do this in the field

Pick one evening this week. At your spot or at home, note the official sunset, the time you can no longer see a deer shape at 100 m with binoculars, and the time you need the headlamp. Write all three in the journal. That gap is your real last light.
